digest.component_or_area: LLM review operations / CLI command aliasing
propositions: The single-pass `rebar review` CLI verb and its library/MCP surfaces are superseded by the multi-pass `review-plan` gate (from above) and deterministic check ops (from below), and must be retired safely via deprecation.

The `rebar review` CLI command must become a loud forwarding shim that aliases to `review-plan` while rejecting unsupported arguments (`--graph`, positional `reviewer_id`) with exit code 2 and names the replacement, rather than silently discarding them.

The deprecated CLI and MCP surfaces must signal through the central `_deprecations.REGISTRY` using scheduled rows (removal in v1.0.0), while the library function `rebar.llm.review_ticket` splits into a private `_review_ticket_impl` (no warning) and a public facade (emits `DeprecationWarning`), so internal callers (MCP tool, diff harness, eval solver) emit exactly one signal per entry point.

The read-only contract of the old verb (no signed attestation) must be preserved by forwarding `--no-sign=True` to `review-plan`, while documented behavioral divergences (fast-fail on non-claimable tickets, multi-pass cost, blocking floor enforcement) are stated in help text and tested.

The output schema key `"review"` must be repointed from `REVIEW_RESULT` to `PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT`, and `REVIEW_RESULT` must be re-wired under a synthetic `"review_ticket"` key for the surviving library/MCP operation, so no schema is orphaned and the shim's output is never misdescribed.

All derived artifacts (prompt index from front-matter, CLI reference from generator script, MCP reference from docstrings, packaged prompt as writer fixed point) must remain in sync with their sources, and hand-authored docs (llm-framework.md, output-schemas.md, AGENTS.md) must be corrected to mark the verb deprecated and name the replacement.
